symptom.observed: A second /v1/responses request entered the same 5555 listener/session before the first SSE response completed, then provider projections failed with malformed function_call_output or an empty message role.
symptom.expected: A listener must admit at most one active Responses request for the same explicit session or conversation scope until its response body reaches EOF, errors, or is dropped.

hypotheses.cause: The V3 listener has no same-session in-flight admission lock, allowing a Codex retry carrying partial stream history to enter Runtime/provider wire concurrently.
hypotheses.supporting_evidence: Requests 16048 and 16063 share port/session and overlap by about 78 seconds; the Codex rollout writes partial reasoning before retry construction.
hypotheses.counter_evidence_or_gap: A controlled overlap test must prove the second request reaches provider before the fix.
hypotheses.verification_action: Run two controlled same-listener/same-session Requests while the first upstream response body is held open and observe provider captures.

hypotheses.cause: V3 HTTP SSE lacks V2-equivalent keepalive comments, leaving an idle transport interval that can trigger client retry behavior.
hypotheses.supporting_evidence: V2 writes an immediate keepalive and repeats every 3000ms; V3 Direct and Relay use Body::from_stream without the existing keepalive builder.
hypotheses.counter_evidence_or_gap: Keepalive alone does not explain every observed retry timeout and cannot replace admission control.
hypotheses.verification_action: Hold a controlled provider SSE body idle and assert immediate plus periodic comment frames without semantic event mutation.
